title: Relative-modular cocycle and resolvent Cook bridge
question: Can a phase-local relative modular cocycle on a resolvent core replace the all-history norm estimate by a summable boundary Cook criterion, while preserving both orientations and the Hamiltonian generator?
status: PROPOSED BREAKTHROUGH ROUTE; NO PROOF GATE CLOSED

new_perspective.core_move: Resum the entire finite-volume difference into one relative cocycle before taking a state-weighted norm. Do not estimate each split-product history separately and do not require a point-norm limit on raw configuration multipliers.
new_perspective.carrier: Use the finite-support oscillator resolvent core R0 generated by R_z(f)=(z-phi(f))^(-1) with Im(z) nonzero, completed in a fixed-beta phase-mixture GNS two-sided L2 topology.
new_perspective.relative_cocycle: For H_prime=H+B define U_prime,H(t)=exp(i t H_prime) exp(-i t H). Then alpha_prime_t(A)=U_prime,H(t) alpha_t(A) U_prime,H(t)^*, and dU/dt=i alpha_prime_t(B) U.
new_perspective.localization: Apply the phase-local conditional expectation to the boundary commutator before the norm. The bulk cancels in B=H_prime-H, while pure-bond layers are tested only through their local shell response.
new_perspective.state_weight: Measure the two orientations with the mixture GNS norm ||X||_2^2=phi(X^*X)+phi(XX^*) and use the relative-modular/BKM form for the cocycle derivative; this is weaker than point norm and does not inherit the raw-Weyl jump.
why_not_duplicate: R-384 splits a finite spectral shell but still leaves the low-frequency M0 modulus and does not resum histories.
The EXP-001203 folded-Renyi route squares a local likelihood and requires a positive Keldysh-to-Euclidean domination; this route never assumes that positivity.
The earlier R306 resolvent-smoothed cylinder is a fixed-support form bridge; this route uses relative cocycles to compare nested volumes and target direct D,delta-D Cauchy.

conditional_bridge.boundary_coefficient: For every local A in R0 and compact time interval |t|<=T, construct b_A(r)>=0 such that the phase-local conditional expectation of the boundary cocycle commutator at shell r is at most C_(A,z,T) b_A(r) in both L2 orientations.
conditional_bridge.summability: The required uniform input is sup_(Lambda subset Lambda_prime,source,cutoff,shape) sum_(r>=0) b_A(r)<infinity, with the same estimate for A^* and for the modular derivative.
conditional_bridge.cook_conclusion: Under those two inputs, the cocycle Duhamel integral gives a uniform strong-star Cauchy bound for alpha_t^Lambda(A) Omega_beta and its adjoint. The resolvent identity R_z(A)-R_z(C)=R_z(A)(C-A)R_z(C) supplies product and inverse bookkeeping on R0.
conditional_bridge.common_alpha_step: If the b_A are phase-independent and the finite embeddings agree on R0, the Cauchy limits obey the cocycle equation, group law and strong continuity on the completed carrier. The phasewise OS functionals can then be tested as normal beta-KMS states of the same limit dynamics.
conditional_bridge.hard_premise: The actual Q3LOCK estimate for b_A(r), including cutoff removal, source uniformity, all-shape geometry and a noncollapsing phase-mixture representation, is not proved by this route design.

finite_checkpoint.planned_test: On the existing Q3 edge and square fixtures, compare H and H+B for one added bond, compute U_prime,H(t), the two orientation state-weighted commutator of B with resolvent-smoothed local seeds, and the cocycle composition residual for both time signs.
finite_checkpoint.coverage: The first implementation must include both beta values, all translated local sites, both split orders, every prefix and both adjoints before any finite result is promoted.
finite_checkpoint.promotion_rule: A finite pass can validate only the cocycle algebra and the chosen weighted observable; it cannot establish b_A summability, a thermodynamic limit, common alpha, KMS/GNS, a gap or QFT closure.
finite_checkpoint.lean_policy: No new Lean theorem is claimed at route-design stage. The scalar resolvent difference identity is reused from verification/lean/Tect/R377. A promoted finite cocycle checkpoint must add a new Lean entrypoint and independent mutation lane.

adversarial_review.check: Differentiate the ordered product explicitly and retain both U and U^* orientations; do not replace the relative cocycle by a commuting surrogate.
B is an unbounded boundary polynomial for Q3LOCK, so the cocycle equation must be interpreted on a declared form/resolvent core and cannot use a bounded perturbation theorem without verification.
The bulk cancellation is exact only for nested Hamiltonians with the same local convention; every boundary term and embedding halo must be enumerated.
Two-sided mixture L2 convergence is weaker than point norm and does not automatically imply a representation-independent C-star action; that upgrade remains a separate gate.
A finite shell table or a static Euclidean tail is not an l1 boundary coefficient. If b_A is not summable, this route must stop or be restricted to a proved regime.
Even a common cocycle limit would still require Hamiltonian identification, OS/KMS/GNS passage, a sector gap and the independent C6/Sector-A/Pre-A interfaces.

promotion_criteria: Derive RMC-2 for the actual Q3LOCK local resolvent core with explicit source-, cutoff- and phase-uniform constants.
Prove RMC-3 for every allowed exhaustion shape and both cocycle orientations, including the modular derivative.
Run primary and non-importing independent finite cocycle implementations, a hostile mutation lane and a new Lean cross-check before registering a finite result.
Use the Cook limit only after direct D,delta-D Cauchy, product/core density, embedding compatibility and the group law are all written as separate verified obligations.
Do not promote common alpha or KMS until the exact finite Hamiltonian generator is identified on the limiting resolvent core.
stop_conditions: If the Q3 boundary commutator has a non-summable shell coefficient in either orientation, record the precise growth obstruction and retire only this cocycle route.

If the relative cocycle leaves the phase-local resolvent core or loses the modular derivative under cutoff removal, fall back to the already registered FI-2/local modular-cocycle route without claiming equivalence.
If finite cocycle composition is stable but the embedding maps are not compatible across shapes, retain the categorical finite result and keep spatial common alpha open.
If a bound depends on beta or phase weights, state the restricted regime and do not infer a beta-independent C-star dynamics.

qft_interface.closed_now: A distinct proof decomposition is registered: histories are resummed into a boundary cocycle and estimated in a phase-local two-sided state topology.
qft_interface.open: The BKM boundary estimate, shell summability, cutoff removal, spatial embeddings, direct D,delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS quotient, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary Q3LOCK dynamics route only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, or Clay conclusion is supplied.

formal_integration.lean: not applicable at route-design stage; reuse R377 only

boundary: Claim-nonbearing route design only. It proves no Q3 boundary coefficient, no cocycle summability, no direct D/delta-D Cauchy theorem, no common alpha, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no gap, no continuum, no C6, no Sector-A and no Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The proposed cocycle/resolvent bridge is a falsifiable way to avoid raw point-norm and history-count obstructions. Until RMC-2 and RMC-3 are proved for the exact Q3LOCK family, it is an idea and not a proof advance.
